clue.text: Feature in how to turn a cat into a man

definitions.text: how to turn a cat into a man
definitions.meaning: cut the tail off MANX, a Manx cat, and you are left with MAN

explanation.surface: A quirky how-to article promising to transform a cat into a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as DE-TAIL: remove the last letter of MANX (the tailless Isle of Man cat breed) and it becomes MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is one particular element or aspect of something, which is a feature.

clue.text: He's about to reform Slade without leader

indicators.note: the outer letters sit around the rest, so they come about it

parts.note: taken as the letters H, E, S

indicators.note: Slade is to be reformed, its letters put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A singer plans to reunite the glam rock band Slade but without their frontman.
explanation.walkthrough: Slade are a 1970s British glam rock band. 'He's' gives its three letters, not a pronoun, and the answer nods to the theme, the Headless Horseman of Sleepy Hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something headless lacks a head, and a head is a leader, so it is without one.

clue.text: Principal's lines are sparkling

parts.note: the principal performer is the star; the 's joins it to what follows
RY, short for railway, the lines a train runs on

explanation.surface: A lead dancer's moves are dazzling.
explanation.definitionFit: A starry sky is full of twinkling points of light, so starry means glittering.

clue.text: Erratic motion around Lagrange point as revealed by satellite

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the single letter
erratic means wandering unpredictably, so the word motion is rearranged

parts.note: the five Lagrange points in orbital mechanics are labelled L1 to L5, so L

explanation.surface: An astronomer describes an object wobbling around a Lagrange point, as seen from orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erratic' turns MOTION into MOONIT, and 'around' puts L inside it. The satellite is the Moon, not a spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonlit scene is lit by the Moon, Earth's natural satellite, so it is shown up by it.

clue.text: Romantic grasped style, doffing cap

parts.note: to have got something is to have grasped or understood it

indicators.note: doffing a cap is taking off a hat, so the word loses its top letter

parts.note: chic means stylishness

explanation.surface: A romantic figure seized a stylish look while politely raising a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doffing cap' removes the first letter of CHIC to leave HIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic fiction, with its gloomy castles and heightened emotion, is part of the Romantic movement in literature.

clue.text: Experienced uplifting drugs like 1 down?

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Es, ecstasy tablets
as means like, in the way of
written out as ONE D, D for down

explanation.surface: Someone experienced with mood-raising drugs asks whether they are like a detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns ES into SE. The reference to 1 down is not to its answer but to its label, read as ONE plus D.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasoned campaigner has been toughened by long practice, so is experienced.

clue.text: US party political switch in social trick

indicators.note: a voter switching parties swaps Republican for Democrat inside the word

parts.note: a social is a party or gathering, as is a reception
D for Democrat, one of the two big American parties

explanation.surface: A US politician changing sides is denounced as a cheap trick at a social event.
explanation.walkthrough: The switch is from R (Republican) to D (Democrat), so the R of RECEPTION becomes D.
explanation.definitionFit: A deception is a ruse that misleads someone, just as a trick does.

clue.text: Doctor has odd brown beds

indicators.note: the odd letters, first, third, fifth and so on, are picked out

explanation.surface: A doctor owns some strange brown beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' looks like an adjective about the beds; it picks letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of BROWN BEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bones is slang for a doctor (from sawbones), and the nickname of the Star Trek ship's doctor.

clue.text: Fruity bureaucrats?

parts.note: names both a small citrus fruit and senior civil servants, which share one word

explanation.definitionFit: Mandarins are small oranges and also powerful officials, originally in imperial China, now senior British civil servants.

clue.text: Film in shadow

definitions.meaning: A 1990 film starring Patrick Swayze and Demi Moore
to follow them like a shadow; a faint shadow of something

explanation.surface: A movie set in darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is a shadowy, faint presence, and to ghost is to trail silently, as a shadow does.

clue.text: Contents of tin can once found in South America

indicators.note: the contents are what lies inside the words, so the answer sits within them

explanation.surface: What was inside a tin can was once discovered in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' belongs to the definition: the Inca empire is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were a people whose empire ruled the Andes until the Spanish conquest, so they were once there.

clue.text: Former prime minister's upset, ultimately very tired

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Robert Peel, British Prime Minister in the 1830s and 1840s, with the 's

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: An ex-PM is distressed and, in the end, utterly exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PEELS into SLEEP. Sleepy Hollow is the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleepy is drowsy and ready for bed, as a tired person is.

clue.text: Pub requires no money for a sort of smoothie?

parts.note: an inn is a pub
O, a zero, means none
a cent is a coin, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A pub needs no cash to serve smoothies.
explanation.walkthrough: Innocent is a well-known UK brand of fruit smoothies, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocent is a smoothie brand, and a guileless innocent is also the opposite of a smooth talker.

clue.text: Cloth manufactured by a German and a Scotsman

parts.note: Rudolf Hess, the Nazi deputy leader
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A fabric is made by a German and a Scot working together.
explanation.walkthrough: Hessian is also the word for someone from Hesse, a red herring here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessian is a coarse woven fabric of jute or hemp, used for sacking.

clue.text: Always move different sappers to protect the Queen

indicators.note: the outer letters surround and so guard the inner ones
made different, the letters of move are rearranged

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Soldiers are endlessly redeployed to guard the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' scrambles only 'move'; the sappers' letters follow it unchanged, and the Queen's letters are tucked in after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Evermore means for all time, forever, which is always.

clue.text: A cyclist's greeting, in the main

parts.note: Chris Hoy, the Scottish Olympic track cycling champion; the 's joins him to the definition

explanation.surface: A cyclist calls out hello, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly' but means at sea, the main being the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahoy is the call sailors use to hail another ship, a greeting at sea.

clue.text: Terminal at Heathrow initially breaks rules

indicators.note: the inserted letters break into the word, splitting it open

parts.note: a code is a set of rules

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: At an airport terminal, a passenger flouts regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' suggests an airport building, matching Heathrow; it is the electrode.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathode is the negative electrode of a cell or battery, one of its terminals.

clue.text: Hard Viking decapitated rider

parts.note: H, as on pencils

indicators.note: with its head cut off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a Norseman is a Viking

explanation.surface: A tough Viking had his head cut off by a rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' removes the N of NORSEMAN, a nod to the theme's Headless Horseman.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseman is one who rides a horse, a rider.

clue.text: Sunday? That's right, man

parts.note: Sol, the sun, plus D for day
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone checks if it is Sunday and is told yes, mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunday' splits into SUN (SOL) and DAY (D).
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers are the men of an army, as in officers and men; a man is a private soldier.

clue.text: Rich duke wears spectacles after springtime?

indicators.note: the next piece is placed after the one before

parts.note: a well is a spring, and T stands for time

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: OO, two round lenses
D, the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A wealthy duke puts on his glasses once spring arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' is the sign that OO goes round D, as glasses sit on a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-to-do is prosperous and comfortably off, which is rich.

clue.text: Star setter's raised to finish

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters read upwards

parts.note: hair gel is a setter, it sets the hair; the 's stands for is
end means finish

explanation.surface: A star crossword compiler has been lifted to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns GEL into LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a celebrated, famous figure, a star in their field.

clue.text: 'Preach to choir!' minister to roar, ultimately in shock

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so each word gives its last letter

explanation.surface: A minister urged to roar a sermon to the faithful ends up in shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Horror is intense fear or dismay, a strong shock to the feelings.

clue.text: 75% of prison is empty

indicators.note: three quarters of the word are kept, six letters of the eight, from the front

parts.note: Holloway was a women's prison in north London

explanation.surface: Most of a prison stands empty.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLLOWAY is a former London women's prison; 75% drops its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hollow has nothing inside it, so it is empty.

clue.text: Fabulous story involves English travel card?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the inserted one
fabulous suggests something made up, so the word story is reworked

explanation.surface: A tall tale features an English ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' turns STORY into OYSTR, which 'involves' puts round E. The Oyster card is London's smart travel pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Oyster is the name of London's contactless smart card for buses and the Underground.

clue.text: Love playing game to the end

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: playing about with the word game rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: A lover keeps playing a game right up to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' turns GAME into MEGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so it stands for the end, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: 'e led Wise's production of a song

indicators.note: a production makes something new out of the letters given

explanation.surface: A man, in Cockney speech, directed a production of a song by Wise.
explanation.walkthrough: Wise may suggest Ernie Wise of the comedy duo Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a song from The Sound of Music, named after the Alpine flower.

clue.text: Derrick's bird

definitions.meaning: a derrick is a lifting ...; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A man named Derrick owns a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A derrick is a kind of hoist used on ships and oil rigs, and a crane is also a tall wading bird.

clue.text: Moved judge jails old king over daughter

indicators.note: the outer word locks the other inside it

parts.note: to rate something is to judge it

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: Old King Cole, the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: A judge imprisons an aged monarch for the sake of his daughter, and has moved.
explanation.walkthrough: The old king is the nursery rhyme's merry Old King Cole; 'over' turns his name round before 'jails' locks it inside the judge's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relocated has been shifted to a new place, so it has moved.
